title: Home first-aid kit checklist
summary: A tickable list of what a household first-aid kit should hold, based on FEMA and Ready.gov lists, plus diabetes-specific items.

sources.title: FEMA - Are You Ready? Appendix B: Disaster Supplies Checklists (first aid supplies)
FEMA / Ready.gov - How to Use a Tourniquet (optional kit item)

blocks.text: This checklist follows FEMA's Are You Ready? disaster supplies list and Ready.gov, with diabetes items added from CDC. Add anything your household's doctors recommend.

items: 3 x 3 inch and 4 x 4 inch sterile gauze pads
CPR breathing barrier such as a face shield
Germicidal hand wipes or waterless alcohol-based hand sanitizer
Pain reliever (see the OTC medicines guide)
Prescription medicines, at least a 7-day supply (CDC), plus a cooler for medicines that need refrigeration
Extra eyeglasses or contact lens supplies
A commercial tourniquet, and know how to use it (see the severe bleeding guide)
Extra gauze or clean cloth for pressure and packing
Glucose tablets or gel and glucagon
Ketone strips, meter and strips, lancets
Insulin supplies and a way to inject (see the T1D go-kit)
Medical ID and copies of prescriptions

blocks.text: Check the kit every 6 months so everything is current and works (CDC). Replace anything that has expired or been used.
